turns.patient_opening: I’m 21, male. I have really bad chest pain—both upper and lower chest—and it also feels like heavy, scary, sickening pain that started very fast. I’m also sweating a lot and I feel very short of breath, and the pain goes to my biceps/shoulders and even my thoracic spine and around the thyroid cartilage, plus I have epigastric pain and right and left breast pain. I’ve also had loss of appetite/early satiety.

turns.doctor_question: What color is the rash? For example, is it **red**, **pink**, **dark**, **pale**, or **yellow**—or is there **no rash**?
turns.patient_answer: I don’t have any rash, so there isn’t a color to describe.

turns.doctor_question: I’m sorry you’re dealing with this. **Do you have any pain somewhere that’s related to the reason you’re consulting today?** (Yes/No)
turns.patient_answer: Yes. The chest pain is the main reason, and it also spreads to my biceps/shoulders and thoracic spine, with epigastric pain and pain around the thyroid cartilage.

turns.doctor_question: When you think about your pain, does it feel **haunting**—like it lingers or won’t let go? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: Yes. It feels like it won’t let go—like it’s lingering and won’t stop.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have pain that gets worse when you move (for example, when you walk, turn, or use the affected area)?
turns.patient_answer: No, it doesn’t get worse with movement like walking or turning. It feels more constant/heavy, not really from using a specific muscle.

turns.doctor_question: Have any of your family members (like a parent, sibling, or child) ever been diagnosed with cluster headaches?
turns.patient_answer: No, I don’t know of any family member diagnosed with cluster headaches.

turns.doctor_question: When you think about your pain, does it feel **sickening** (like nauseating, grim, or deeply unpleasant)? **Yes or no.**
turns.patient_answer: Yes. It feels sickening and deeply unpleasant.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel any pain somewhere in your upper middle abdomen (epigastric area)?
turns.patient_answer: Yes, I have pain in my epigastric area.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel any pain somewhere in your **right breast** right now? (Yes or No)
turns.patient_answer: Yes. I have right breast pain right now.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel any pain somewhere in your **left breast** right now? (Yes or No)
turns.patient_answer: Yes. I have left breast pain right now.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a heart attack, or do you currently get angina—chest pain or pressure (especially with activity or stress)?
turns.patient_answer: I’ve been told I’ve had angina/chest pain before, so yes—I currently get chest pain/angina.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel the pain, does it feel like a **sudden sharp “knife-like” stab**? (yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: No, it doesn’t feel like a sudden sharp knife-like stab. It feels heavy and sickening.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have swelling in one or more areas of your body? (Yes or no)
Do you have any close family members (like a parent, sibling, or child) who had a cardiovascular problem—such as a heart attack, stroke, or serious heart disease—before the age of 50?

turns.doctor_question: Do you have symptoms that get worse when you’re physically active or exerting yourself, but improve or ease up when you rest? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: No. It doesn’t really get worse with physical activity or exertion, and it doesn’t clearly ease up when I rest.
